name: Partio
listed_description: Library for wrangling particle data, with support for most common file formats.
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline. The README (opened via raw.githubusercontent.com and github.com) only advises using iterators because they are 'much more optimized' than data() and dataAsFloat, a directional internal tip with no numbers; the repo (499 stars) has no benchmark directory and WebSearch found no published read/write speed comparison against BGEO, Alembic or OpenVDB.

name: PDF4QT
listed_description: PDF toolkit with a rendering and editing library, a viewer and command line tools.
reason: No numeric comparison against Poppler, PDFium or any other baseline. README, RELEASES.txt and NOTES.txt (read via raw.githubusercontent.com) mention only unquantified 'Performance optimization' issues (#10, #18) and multithreading; the 1.5k-star repo has no benchmark directory, and a WebSearch for PDF4QT rendering speed against Poppler or PDFium found nothing.

name: PlutoFilter
listed_description: A single-header, zero-allocation image filter library in C.
reason: Directional claim only. The README says 'fast, chainable image effects' with no numbers and no baseline; the repo (203 stars, MIT) has examples/ and tests/ holding 67 reference images but no timing code, and WebSearch found no PlutoFilter versus OpenCV or libvips benchmark.

name: PoDoFo
listed_description: A library to work with the PDF file format.
reason: No numeric comparison against any baseline. github.com/podofo/podofo (611 stars, LGPL-2.0-or-later or MPL-2.0) README and CHANGELOG.md carry only unquantified performance notes (garbage collection rewritten with a stack, PdfPageCollection rewritten for performance); issue #108 is a regression report with no timings and no other library; PoDoFo is absent from the pdq crate's qpdf, MuPDF and Poppler merge timings that WebSearch surfaced; no shootout including PoDoFo was found.

name: PortAudio
listed_description: PortAudio is a free, cross-platform, open-source, audio I/O library.
reason: No numeric comparison against a named baseline. github.com/PortAudio/portaudio (2.2k stars) README and tree show only test/pa_minlat.c, a minimum-latency tool for one's own machine; WebSearch found a single-machine 72 ms macOS round-trip anecdote, a Stack Overflow anecdote of 5 to 10 ms with ASIO and no head-to-head latency or throughput numbers against RtAudio, miniaudio, libsoundio, SDL or OpenAL.
